hints: The horizontal parts of the force are the same in both cases. What differs, and by how much?
worded:
1. The forward component F cos 30° is the same in both cases, so only the friction differs.

2. Pushing down adds F sin 30° = 10 N to N; pulling up removes 10 N. The normal forces are 60 N and 40 N.

3. The friction differs by 0.2 × 20 = 4 N, so the accelerations differ by 4/5 = 0.8 m/s². (C)

4. Check that both slide: 17.3 N exceeds 12 N and 8 N, so kinetic friction applies in both cases.

**No-pen route.** Δa = μ × (difference in N)/m = 0.2 × 2F sin 30°/5 = 0.2 × 20/5 = 0.8 m/s².
